verses.text: And these are the words of the book, which Baruch the son of Nerias, the son of Maasias, the son of Sedecias, the son of Asadias, the son of Chelcias, wrote in Babylon,
In the fift yere, and in the seventh day of the moneth, what time as the Caldeans tooke Jerusalem, and burnt it with fire.
And Baruch did reade the words of this book, in the hearing of Iechonias, the son of Ioachim king of Judah, and in the eares of all the people, that came to the book.

And in the hearing of the nobles, and of the kings sons, and in the hearing of the Elders, and of all the people from the lowest to the highest, even of all them that dwelt at Babylon, by the riuer Sud.
Whereupon they wept, fasted, and prayed before the Lord.
They made also a collection of money, according to every mans power.
And they sent it to Jerusalem to Ioachim the hie Priest the son of Chelcias, son of Salom, and to the Priests, and to all the people which were found with him at Jerusalem,

At the same time, when he received the vessels of the house of the Lord that were caried out of the Temple, to returne them into the land of Judah the tenth day of the moneth Siuan, siluer vessels, which Sedecias the son of Iosias king of Judah had made,
After that Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon had caried away Iechonias, and the Princes, and the captives, and the mighty men, and the people of the land from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon:
And they said, Behold, we have sent you money, to buy you burnt offerings, and sin offerings, and incense, and prepare you Manna, and offer upon the Altar of the Lord our Alahayam,
And pray for the life of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and for the life of Balthasar his son, that their days may be upon earth as the days of heaven.

And the Lord will give us strength, and lighten our eyes, and we shall live under the shadow of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and under the shadow of Balthasar his son, and we shall serve them many days, and find favor in their sight.
Pray for us also to the Lord our Alahayam, (for we have sinned against the Lord our Alahayam, and to this day the fury of the Lord, and his wrath is not turned from us)
And you shall reade this book, which we have sent to you, to make confession in the house of the Lord, upon the feasts and solemne days.
And you shall say, To the Lord our Alahayam belongs righteousness, but to us the confusion of faces, as it is come to pass this day to them of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
And to our kings, and to our princes, and to our Priests, and to our Prophets, and to our fathers.
For we have sinned before the Lord,
And disobeyed him, and have not hearkened to the voice of the Lord our Alahayam, to walk in the commandments that he gave us openly:

Since the day that the Lord brought our forefathers out of the land of Egypt, to this present day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our Alahayam, and we have been negligent in not hearing his voice.

Therefore the evils cleaued to us, and the curse which the Lord appointed by Moses his servant, at the time that he brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt, to give us a land that flows with milke and honie, like as it is to see this day.
Nevertheless we have not hearkened to the voice of the Lord our Alahayam, according to all the words of the Prophets, whom he sent to us.
But every man followed the imagination of his own wicked heart, to serve strange gods, and to do evil in the sight of the Lord our Alahayam.

Therefore the Lord has made good his word, which he pronounced against us, and against our Judges that iudged Yahsharala, and against our kings, and against our princes, and against the men of Yahsharala and Judah,
To bring upon us great plagues, such as never happened under the whole heaven, as it came to pass in Jerusalem, according to the things that were written in the Law of Moses,
That a man should eat the flesh of his own son, and the flesh of his own daughter.
Moreouer, he has deliuered them to be in subiection to all the kingdoms that are round about us, to be as a reproch and desolation among all the people round about, where the Lord has scattered them.
Thus we were cast downe and not exalted, because we have sinned against the Lord our Alahayam, and have not been obedient to his voice.
To the Lord our Alahayam belongs righteousness: but to us and to our fathers open shame, as appears this day.
For all these plagues are come upon us, which the Lord has pronounced against us,
Yet have we not prayed before the Lord, that we might turne every one from the imaginations of his wicked heart.
Therefore the Lord watched over us for evil, and the Lord has brought it upon us: for the Lord is righteous in all his works, which he has commanded us.
Yet we have not hearkened to his voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord, that he has set before us.

And now O Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala, that have brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and high arm, and with signes and with wonders, and with great power, and have gotten your selfe a name, as appears this day:
O Lord our Alahayam, we have sinned, we have done ungodly, we have dealt vnrighteously in all your ordinances.
Let your wrath turne from us: for we are but a few left among the heathen, where you have scattered us.
Hear our prayers, O Lord, and our petitions, and deliuer us for your own sake, and give us favor in the sight of them which have led us away:
That all the earth may know that you are the Lord our Alahayam, because Yahsharala and his posterity is called by your name.
O Lord look downe from your holy house, and consider us: bow downe your eare, O Lord, to hear us.
Open your eyes and behold: for the dead that are in the graues, whose souls are taken from their bodies, will give to the Lord neither praise nor righteousness.
But the soul that is greatly vexed, which goes stouping and feeble, and the eyes that faile, and the hungry soul will give you praise and righteousnes O Lord.
Therfore we do not make our humble supplication before you, O Lord our Alahayam, for the righteousnes of our fathers, and of our kings.
For you have sent out your wrath and indignation upon us, as you have spoken by your servants the prophets, saying,
Thus says the Lord, bow down your shoulders to serve the king of Babylon: so shall you remain in the lande that I gave to your fathers.
But if you will not hear the voice of the Lord to serve the king of Babylon,

I will cause to cease out of the cities of Judah, and from without Jerusalem the voice of mirth, and the voice of ioy: the voice of the bridegrome, and the voice of the bride, and the whole land shall be desolate of inhabitants.

But we would not hearken to your voyce, to serve the king of Babylon: therefore have you made good the words that you spoke by your servants the prophets, namely that the bones of our kings, and the bones of our fathers should be taken out of their places.
And loe, they are cast out to the heat of the day, and to the frost of the night, and they died in great miseries, by famine, by sword, and by pestilence.
And the house which is called by your name (have you laid waste) as it is to be seene this day, for the wickednesse of the house of Yahsharala, and the house of Judah.
O Lord our Alahayam, you have dealt with us after all your goodness, and according to all that great mercy of yours.
As you spoke by your servant Moses in the day when you did command him to write your Law, before the children of Yahsharala, saying,
If you will not hear my voyce, surely this very great multitude shalbe turned into a smal among the nations, where I will scatter them.
For I knew that they would not hear me: because it is a stiffenecked people: but in the land of their captiuities, they shall remember themselues,
And shall know that I am the Lord their Alahayam: For I give them an heart, and eares to hear.
And they shall praise me in the land of their captiuitie, and thinke upon my name,
And returne from their stiffe neck, and from their wicked deeds: for they shall remember the way of their fathers which sinned before the Lord.

And I will bring them again into the land which I promised with an oath to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be lords of it, and I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished.
And I will make an everlasting couenant with them, to be their Alahayam, and they shall be my people: and I will no more driue my people of Yahsharala out of the land that I have given them.
O Lord almighty, Alahayam of Yahsharala, the soul in anguish, the troubled spirit crieth to you.
Hear O Lord, and have mercy: for you are mercifull, and have pitty upon us, because we have sinned before you.
For you endure for ever, and we perish vtterly.

O Lord almighty, you Alahayam of Yahsharala, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before you, and not hearkened to the voice of you their Alahayam: for the which cause these plagues cleaue to us.
Remember not the iniquities of our forefathers: but thinke upon your power and your name, now at this time.
For you are the Lord our Alahayam, and you, O Lord, will we praise.

And for this cause you have put your fear in our hearts, to the intent that we should call upon your name, and praise you in our captiuity: for we have called to minde all the iniquity of our forefathers that sinned before you.

Behold, we are yet this day in our captiuity, where you have scattered us, for a reproch and a curse, and to be subiect to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers which departed from the Lord our Alahayam.
Hear, Yahsharala, the commandments of life, give eare to understand wisdom.
How happens it, Yahsharala, that you are in your enemies land, that you are waxen old in a strange country, that you are defiled with the dead?
That you are counted with them that go downe into the graue?
You have forsaken the fountaine of wisdom.
For if you had walked in the way of Alahayam, you should have dwelled in peace for ever.
Learne where is wisdom, where is strength, where is understanding, that you may know also where is length of days, and life, where is the light of the eyes and peace.
Who has found out her place? or who has come into her treasures?
Where are the princes of the heathen become, and such as ruled the beasts upon the earth.
They that had their pastime with the foules of the aire, and they that hoorded up siluer and gold wherein men trust, and made no end of their getting?
For they that wrought in siluer, and were so carefull, and whose workes are vnsearchable,
They are vanished, and gone downe to the graue, and others are come up in their steads.
Young men have seene light, and dwelt upon the earth: but the way of knowledge have they not known,
Nor understood the pathes thereof; nor laid hold of it: their children were farre off from that way.
It has not been heard of in Chanaan: neither has it been seene in Theman.

The Agarenes that seek wisdome upon earth, the marchants of Merran, and of Theman, the authors of fables, and searchers out of understanding: none of these have known the way of wisdom, or remember her pathes.
O Yahsharala, how great is the house of Alahayam? and how large is the place of his possession?
Great, and has none end: high, and vnmeasurable.
There were the gyants, famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.
Those did not the Lord chuse, neither gave he the way of knowledge to them.
But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishnesse.
Who has gone up into heaven and taken her, and brought her downe from the clouds?
Who has gone over the Sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold?
No man knows her way, nor thinks of her path.
But he that knows all things, knows her, and has found her out with his understanding: he that prepared the earth for evermore, has filled it with fourefooted beasts.
He that sends forth light, and it goes: calls it again, and it obeys him with fear.
The starres shined in their watches, and rejoiced: when he calls them, they say, Here we be, and so with cheerefulnesse they showed light to him that made them.
This is our Alahayam, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him.
He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yahsharala his beloued.
Afterward did he show himselfe upon earth, and conuersed with men.
This is the Book of the commandments of Alahayam: and the Law that endures for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life: but such as leave it, shall die.
Turne you, O Jacob, and take heed of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof, that you may be illuminated.
Give not your honor to another, nor the things that are profitable to you, to a strange nation.
O Yahsharala, happie are we: for things that are pleasing to Alahayam, are made known to us.
Be of good cheare, my people, the memoriall of Yahsharala.
you were sold to the nations, not for destruction: but because you moved Alahayam to wrath, you were deliuered to the enemies.
For you prouoked him that made you, by sacrificing to deuils, and not to Alahayam.
You have forgotten the everlasting Alahayam, that brought you up, and you have grieved Jerusalem that noursed you.
For when she saw the wrath of Alahayam coming upon you, she said; Hearken, O you that dwell about Sion: Alahayam has brought upon me great mourning.
For I saw the captiuitie of my sons and daughters, which the everlasting brought upon them.
With ioy did I nourish them: but sent them away with weeping and mourning.
Let no man rejoice over me a widow, and forsaken of many, who for the sins of my children, am left desolate: because they departed from the Law of Alahayam.
They knew not his statutes, nor walked in the waies of his Commandments, nor trode in the pathes of discipline in his righteousness.
Let them that dwell about Sion come, and remember you the captiuity of my sons and daughters, which the everlasting has brought upon them.
For he has brought a nation upon them from far: a shamelesse nation, and of a strange language, who neither reuerenced old man, nor pitied childe.
These have caried away the dear beloued children of the widow, and left her that was alone, desolate without daughters.
But what can I helpe you?
For he that brought these plagues upon you, will deliuer you from the hands of your enemies.
Go your way, O my children, go your way: for I am left desolate.
I have put off the clothing of peace, and put upon me the sackcloth of my prayer. I will cry to the everlasting in my days.
Be of good cheare, O my children, cry to the Lord: and he shall deliuer you from the power and hand of the enemies.
For my hope is in the Everlasting that he will saue you, and ioy is come to me from the Holy one, because of the mercy which shall soone come to you from the everlasting our Sauiour.
For I sent you out with mourning and weeping: but Alahayam will give you to me again, with ioy and gladnesse for ever.

Like as now the neighbours of Sion have seene your captiuity: so shall they see shortly your saluation from our Alahayam, which shall come upon you with great glory, and brightnesse of the everlasting.
My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from Alahayam: for your enemy has persecuted you: but shortly you shall see his destruction, and shall tread upon his necke.
My delicate ones have gone rough ways, and were taken away as a flocke caught of the enemies.
Be of good comfort, O my children, and cry to Alahayam: for you shall be remembred of him that brought these things upon you.
For as it was your minde to go astray from Alahayam: so being returned seeke him ten times more.
For he that has brought these plagues upon you, shall do you bring everlasting ioy again with your saluation.
Take a good heart, O Jerusalem: for he that gave you that name, will comfort you.
Miserable are they that afflicted you, and rejoiced at your fall.
Miserable are the cities which your children served: miserable is she that received your sons.
For as she rejoiced at your ruine, and was glad of your fall: so shall she be grieved for her own desolation.
For I will take away the reioycing of her great multitude, and her pride shalbe turned into mourning.
For fire shall come upon her from the everlasting, long to endure: and she shall be inhabited of deuils for a great time.
O Jerusalem, look about you toward the East, and behold the ioy that comes to you from Alahayam.
Loe, your sons come whom you sent away: they come gathered together from the East to the West, by the word of the holy One, reioycing in the glory of Alahayam.
Put off, O Jerusalem, the garment of your mourning and affliction, and put on the comelinesse of the glory that comes from Alahayam for ever.
Cast about you a double garment of the righteousness which comes from Alahayam, and set a diademe on your head of the glory of the everlasting.
For Alahayam will show your brightnesse to every country under heaven.
For your name shall be called of Alahayam for ever, The peace of righteousness, and the glory of Gods worship.

Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the East, and behold your children gathered from the West to the East by the word of the holy One, reioycing in the remembrance of Alahayam.
For they departed from you on foote, and were ledde away of their enemies: but Alahayam brings them to you exalted with glory, as children of the kingdom.

For Alahayam has appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance should be cast downe, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Yahsharala may go safely in the glory of Alahayam.
Moreouer, even the woods, and every sweet smelling tree, shall ouershadow Yahsharala by the commandment of Alahayam.
For Alahayam shall leade Yahsharala with ioy, in the light of his glory, with the mercy and righteousnes that comes from him.
A copy of an Epistle which Ieremie sent to them which were to be led captives into Babylon, by the king of the Babylonians, to certifie them as it was commanded him of Alahayam.
Because of the sins which you have committed before Alahayam, you shall be led away captives to Babylon by Nabuchodonosor king of the Babylonians.
So when you be come to Babylon, you shall remain there many years, and for a long season, namely seven generations: and after that I will do you bring away peaceably from thence.
Now shall you see in Babylon gods of siluer, and of gold, and of wood, borne upon shoulders, which cause the nations to fear.
Beware therefore that you in no wise be like to strangers, neither be you afraid of them, when you see the multitude before them, and behinde them, worshipping them.
But say you in your hearts, O Lord, we must worship you.
For mine Angel is with you, and I my selfe caring for your souls.
As for their tongue, it is polished by the workeman, and they themselues are guilded and laid over with siluer, yet are they but false and cannot speak.
And taking golde, as it were for a virgine that loues to go gay, they make crownes for the heads of their gods.
Sometimes also the Priests conuey from their gods golde and siluer, and bestow it upon themselues.
Yea they will give thereof to the common harlots, and decke them as men with garments gods of siluer, and gods of gold, and wood.
Yet cannot these gods saue themselues from rust and moths, though they be couered with purple raiment.
They wipe their faces because of the dust of the Temple, when there is much upon them.
And he that cannot put to death one that offends him, holds a scepter as though he were a judge of the country.
He has also in his right hand a dagger, and an axe: but cannot deliuer himselfe from war and theeues.
Whereby they are known not to be gods, therefore fear them not.

For like as a vessell that a man uses, is nothing worth when it is broken: even so it is with their gods: when they be set up in the Temple, their eyes be full of dust, thorow the feet of them that come in.

And as the doores are made sure on every side, upon him that offends the king, as being committed to suffer death: even so the priests make fast their temples, with doores, with lockes and barres, lest their gods be spoiled with robbers.
They light them candles, yea, more then for themselues, whereof they cannot see one.
They are as one of the beames of the temple, yet they say, their hearts are gnawed upon by things creeping out of the earth, and when they eat them and their clothes, they feele it not.
Their faces are blacked, thorow the smoke that comes out of the temple.
Upon their bodies and heads, sit battes, swallowes, and birds, and the cats also.
By this you may know that they are no gods: therefore fear them not.
Notwithstanding the gold that is about them, to make them beautifull, except they wipe off the rust they will not shine: for neither when they were molten did they feele it.
The things wherein there is no breath, are bought for a most hie price.
They are borne upon shoulders, having no feete, whereby they declare to men that they be nothing worth.

They also that serve them, are ashamed: for if they fall to the ground at any time, they cannot rise up again of themselues: neither if one set them upright can they move of themselues: neither if they be bowed downe, can they make themselues streight: but they set gifts before them as to dead men.
As for the things that are sacrificed to them, their priests sell and abuse: in like manner their wiues lay up part thereof in salt: but to the poor and impotent, they give nothing of it.
Menstruous women, and women in childbed eat their sacrifices: by these things you may know that they are no gods: fear them not.
For how can they be called gods? because women set food before the gods of siluer, gold, and wood.
And the priests sit in their temples, having their clothes rent, and their heads and beards shauen, and nothing upon their heads.
They roare and crie before their gods: as men do at the feast when one is dead.
The priests also take off their garments, and clothe their wiues and children.
Whether it be evil that one does to them, or good: they are not able to recompense it: they can neither set up a king, nor put him downe.
In like manner, they can neither give riches nor money: though a man make a vowe to them, and keep it not, they will not require it.
They can saue no man from death, neither deliuer the weake from the mighty.
They cannot restore a blind man to his sight, nor helpe any man in his distresse.
They can show no mercy to the widow: nor do good to the fatherlesse.
Their gods of wood, and which are ouerlaid with gold, and siluer, are like the stones that be hewen out of the mountaine: they that worship them shall be confounded.
How should a man then thinke and say that they are gods? when even the Chaldeans themselves dishonor them.
Who if they shall see one dumbe that cannot speak, they bring him and intreate Bel that he may speak, as though he were able to understand.
Yet they cannot understand this themselues, and leave them: for they have no knowledge.

The women also with cordes above them, sitting in the ways, burne branne for perfume: but if any of them drawen by some that passes by, lie with him, she reproaches her fellow that she was not thought as worthy as her selfe, nor her cord broken.
Whatever is done among them is false: how may it then be thought or said that they are gods?
They are made of carpenters, and goldsmiths, they can be nothing else, then the workman will have them to be.
And they themselues that made them, can never continue long, how should then the things that are made of them, be gods?
For they left lies and reproaches to them that come after.
For when there comes any war or plague upon them, the priests consult with themselues, where they may be hidden with them.
How then cannot men perceiue, that they be no gods, which can neither saue themselues from war nor from plague?
For seeing they be but of wood, and ouerlaide with siluer and gold: it shall be known heereafter that they are false.
And it shall manifestly appeare to all nations and kings, that they are no gods: but the workes of mens hands, and that there is no worke of Alahayam in them.
Who then may not know that they are no gods?
For neither can they set up a king in the land, nor give raine to men.
Neither can they judge their own cause, nor redresse a wrong being vnable: for they are as crowes between heaven and earth.
Whereupon when fire falls upon the house of gods of wood, or layd over with gold or siluer, their priests will fly away, and escape: but they themselues shall be burnt asunder like beames.
Moreouer they cannot withstand any king or enemies: how can it then be thought or said that they be gods?
Neither are those gods of wood, and layd over with siluer or gold able to escape either from theeues or robbers.
Whose gold, and siluer, and garments wherwith they are clothed, they that are strong do take, and take them away: neither are they able to helpe themselues.

Therefore it is better to be a king that shows his power, or else a profitable vessell in an house, which the owner shall have use of, then such false gods: or to be a doore in an house to keep such things safe as be therein, then such false gods: or a pillar of wood in a palace, then such false gods.
For Sunne, Moone, and starres, being bright and sent to do their offices, are obedient.
In like manner the lightning when it breaks forth is easie to be seene, and after the same manner the wind blows in every country.
And when Alahayam commands the clouds to go over the whole world: they do as they are bidden:
And the fire sent from above to consume hilles and woods, does as it is commanded: but these are like to them neither in show, nor power.
Therefore it is neither to be supposed nor said, that they are gods, seeing they are able, neither to judge causes, nor to do good to men.
Knowing therefore that they are no gods, fear them not.
For they can neither curse nor blesse kings.
Neither can they signes in the heavens among the heathen: nor shine as the Sunne, nor give light as the Moone.
The beasts are better then they: for they can get under a couert, and helpe themselues.
It is then by no meanes manifest to us that they are gods: therefore fear them not.
For as a scarcrow in a garden of Cucumbers keeps nothing: so are their gods of wood, and laid over with siluer and gold.
And likewise their gods of wood, and laid over with siluer and gold, are like to a white thorne in an orchard that every bird sits upon: as also to a dead body, that is cast into the darke.
And you shall know them to be no gods, by the bright purple that rots upon them: and they themselues afterward shall be eaten, and shall be a reproach in the country.
Better therefore is the just man that has none idoles: for he shall be farre from reproach.
